body_markdown:
Fun car things: We do them. And so do you, based on the things you share in our ever-busy comments section. This week, we’re exploring automotive events that we haven’t yet crossed off our list. This can mean covering it, participating in it, or just going for fun. Here are a few from our staff; let us know what event is on your bucket list in the comments below.


## 200-mph Club


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


I haven’t gone 200 mph yet—175 is the most I’ve mustered so far, at one of those stock-car lapping things at Talladega. Also, I’ve never done any land-speed anything, be it runways or lakebeds. It’d be nice to change that with a[trip to Bonneville](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorsports/gallery-bonneville-speed-week-2026/) and a seat behind some sort of V-8-powered beast. It’d also be a chance to hang out with Brandan Gillogly, which is always a plus. — *Eddy Eckart*


## The Race of Gentlemen


Sean Smith


One day, I’d love to go see[The Race of Gentlemen](https://www.hagerty.com/media/magazine-features/sand-blasting-the-race-of-gentlemen-honors-classic-hot-rods-at-the-jersey-shore/) . A period car show and race festival on the beach, with old-school hot rods and gassers, is exactly the kind of goofball celebration we need more of. Not to mention I’m an east coaster with a soft spot for beach towns like Wildwood, New Jersey, where the event takes place. Fitting that a vintage car event be held in a town with aging waterfront motels and rickety wooden roller coasters. Give me a hot dog, some salt water taffy, caramel popcorn, and cheap lagers in a cooler. — *Eric Weiner*


## Retromobile Paris


[Ronan Glon](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/rglon/)


I’ve been lucky enough to participate in and spectate some wonderful events across the U.S., so I’m going to reach here and go with an event multiple friends have traveled to and come home with great stories: Paris Retromobile.


From the sounds of things, Retromobile has a laid-back vibe and phenomenal cars. The tales have convinced me to even try to learn a little French just in case one of the airlines accidentally books me a flight that works perfectly with the early February dates next year. A boy can dream, right? — *Kyle Smith*


## Le Mans


Corbis/VCG/Getty Images


This isn’t the most creative answer, but I’ve got to do Le Mans before I kick it. I’ve been reading and writing about cars that raced there for a long time, so daydreaming about the race comes naturally. The camping and partying with friends in between all the race-watching sounds right up my alley, and then when it’s all done there are countless other car things to do that are a train ride or a cheap plane ticket away. — *Andrew Newton*


## Corvette Ownership


Unsplash/Richard Goff


I really want to run the New Balance 250, which is the first tank of gas you burn through in your first Corvette. — *Brandan Gillogly*


## Off-roading on Safari


[Eddy Eckart](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/eeckarthagerty-com/)


[Eddy Eckart](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/eeckarthagerty-com/)


This is an oddball wish, but I have been fortunate enough to check a lot of car-related boxes. Except one, and it really isn’t a specific car event: One place I’ve never had the chance to visit is Africa, and it’s been a dream to see, and hopefully photograph, lions and elephants and other inhabitants of the veldt. I know there are plenty of safari trips offered up online—and the fact that I just searched them on Google means I will be getting a steady stream of visit-Africa ads on my Facebook page; I’d just have to do it my so I’d feel I felt I was getting maximum “Daktari,” a CBS TV series from my childhood that exposed me to the aforementioned lions and tigers and, just as important, Land Rovers and Jeep J-10s… — *Steven Cole Smith*


## Cruisin’ California


Hagerty


I’m an absolute sucker for a good road trip, particularly one that incorporates beautiful scenery of all types—coast, mountains, grasslands, I love it all. While I’m content making long journeys without a gaggle of other vehicles along for the ride, I won’t deny the appeal of several machines chasing the same beautiful roads together. I think it would be incredible to drive the California Mille someday. Sure, the vehicles that star in that event may be a bit out of my price range, but dreaming is free, and those roads look about as good as they get. If I had my druthers, pop me behind the wheel of a Porsche 356 Speedster or a sleek Jaguar with a silky straight-six and let me soak in the sun, the mountain views, and the gorgeous California coastline. — *Nathan Petroelje*
